extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism/stability/resistance evidence from XML sections, methods, and figure captions.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper uses prior HPA3NT3-A2 evidence that the peptide penetrates the bacterial membrane, binds nucleic acids, and inhibits protein synthesis; this is retained only as cited mechanism context, not a new direct assay in this paper.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The direct nucleic-acid/protein-synthesis evidence is attributed to cited prior work rather than newly quantified in this source paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD and SUV liposome assays support a membrane-interaction contrast: HPA3NT3 shows stronger interaction/alpha-helical structure with PE/PG and PC/SM vesicles, while HPA3NT3-A2 and HPA3NT3-A2D show low levels of alpha-helical structure in those liposome conditions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure curves are used qualitatively; exact spectral/binding coordinates are not text-extracted or invented.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Replacing all L-Lys residues in HPA3NT3-A2 with D-Lys residues is source-supported as a stability strategy; HPLC serum incubation and serum antimicrobial assays support improved resistance to proteolytic degradation while retaining antimicrobial activity.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Only source-stated ranges/trends are preserved; exact figure-only curve points are not fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Serial-passage MIC testing in Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923 supports the paper claim that HPA3NT3-A2/HPA3NT3-A2D did not induce detectable resistance over the reported passages, unlike rifampin comparator behavior.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure 6 relative MIC curve values are not digitized; the qualitative no-resistance conclusion is source-supported.
